Resting for games, made more exact.

- A game is recognised by the program that's running, not by anything passed to it. A terminal command or an editor that only mentions a game's folder no longer makes the wallpaper rest.
- A graphics card that's asleep (a laptop's second one, say) isn't woken every couple of seconds to ask how busy it is. Asleep, it's idle anyway.

Checked on Linux, with RaceRoom running under Proton: the wallpaper rested (1.7% of a core, against about 10% while it moves), and it carried on again once the game was gone. The game's program path matches either way, so 1.24.0 rested for it too.
